# The MemCorrect corpus is generated by a seeded, schema-validated generator and pinned by content hash

Status: accepted

## Context
The MemCorrect benchmark (issue #1584) needs scenarios that exercise correction uptake, scoping, anti-events, collateral damage, and re-assertion - on a corpus that is deterministic, free of real user data, and stable enough that a committed hash means something. Hand-built or generated-on-the-fly corpora drift; a digest over a subset would let limited runs disagree; twins and collateral facts seeded in the wrong order make scope_precision and collateral_delta unmeasurable (they measure nothing if the twin does not yet exist or the fact was never stored).

Theme consolidation: this record merges 11 sweep themes into one decision family (57 origin records): memcorrect-anti-events, memcorrect-collateral-probes, memcorrect-corpus-generation, memcorrect-dataset-hashing, memcorrect-establishing-transcripts, memcorrect-explicit-schema-validation, memcorrect-no-pii-token-pools, memcorrect-runtime-schema-validation, memcorrect-scoped-fixtures, memcorrect-seeded-determinism, memcorrect-timing-invariants.

## Decision
- The corpus is produced by a deterministic seeded generator (Mulberry32 PRNG, same contract as the retention-aged fixture generator) over synthetic token pools containing no PII.
- Every persona owns at least two namespaces (work + home) so scoped scenarios can seed a twin in the alternate namespace; the twin is seeded BEFORE the correction so scope_precision can catch a system that applies the correction across namespaces (the twin must already exist to be overwritten).
- Each scenario carries a two-turn establishing transcript in which both turns carry the original value, so deduplicating or summarizing systems still capture it; the re-assertion scenario's correction is a value the user later walks back, and the reassertion block carries the original.
- One anti-event per scenario, cycling through the three kinds so false_apply exercises each. The anti-event's decoy value is neither the corrected nor the retired value (value pools disjoint by construction), so a correct apply is never mistaken for a false apply; the decoy must not stick from a third-party or hypothetical cue. Anti-event probes are recorded under the post_correction phase with scenario-scoped tokens so cross-scenario leakage cannot inflate the score.
- Collateral facts: two unrelated facts per scenario with distinct subjects (never the main subject nor a prior probe's), each with its own establishing transcript, seeded BEFORE the baseline probe - otherwise collateral_delta recalls facts that were never stored and stays pinned near zero.
- Scenario base times are staggered so timestamps never collide and half-open windows stay unambiguous; only probes strictly after the correction count.
- The generated corpus is validated against an explicit schema (non-empty fields, enum membership, cross-field requirements) before use.
- Dataset identity is a hash over the full served payload - prompt text, memory content, answer tokens, keywords, token costs, skill steps - so any edit that changes what the benchmark serves invalidates the digest; the hash covers ALL scenarios (the run limit only trims which scenarios execute).

## Consequences
Any corpus change is a deliberate repin (new hash). Adding scenario families means updating the schema and the seeded pools. Staggered timestamps constrain scenario scheduling. The no-PII token pools bound how realistic names and values can be.
